name: lsblk
description: Lists block devices (disks, partitions, LVM volumes) as a tree, showing sizes and mount points.

flags.description: Include filesystem type, UUID, and label — the info you need for /etc/fstab.
-all: include empty devices and loop devices.

examples.output:
NAME   MAJ:MIN RM   SIZE RO TYPE MOUNTPOINTS
sda      8:0    0 238.5G  0 disk
├─sda1   8:1    0   512M  0 part /boot/efi
└─sda2   8:2    0   238G  0 part /
nvme0n1 259:0  0 465.8G  0 disk
└─nvme0n1p1 259:1 0 465.8G 0 part /data
examples.explanation: Two physical disks (sda = SATA/SCSI, nvme0n1 = NVMe) with their partition trees and mount points.

examples.output:
NAME  FSTYPE LABEL UUID                                 MOUNTPOINT
sda1  vfat   EFI   4F0B-1A2C                            /boot/efi
sda2  ext4   root  8c1e...-4d2a...                      /
examples.explanation: Filesystem details: type and UUID — copy these into /etc/fstab for reliable mounting.

about: lsblk reads sysfs and presents the block device hierarchy: disks (TYPE disk), partitions (part), LVM volumes (lvm), RAID arrays (md), and loop devices. It never requires root and never touches the devices — it is purely informational, unlike fdisk.
useCases: Identify disks before partitioning or formatting.
mistakes: Confusing device names: nvme0n1p1 is partition 1 of NVMe disk 0; sda1 is partition 1 of disk a.
